qti-choice-interaction.qti-simple-choice: The audit traced the guild's subversion to its own credentialing committee, which had spent a decade quietly passing apprentices who paid and failing those who would not.
Marchers filled the square in open subversion, reading their demands aloud beneath the ministry's windows and daring the clerks to copy every word.
Inspectors catalogued the bridge's subversion plainly: three cables cut in the night, bolts loosened along the north span, and tools abandoned at the waterline.
The committee put the code's subversion down to simple neglect, with forms going unfiled and deadlines sliding until no one could say when the rules had stopped being read.

qti-content-body.p: Correct! Subversion means the weakening or overthrowing of a system from within by quiet, indirect means, so it's the correct answer because the guild's own committee turned the guild's own credentials into merchandise for a decade — no rule visibly broken, and the standard quietly emptied of meaning.
Not quite. Subversion is the quiet turning of a system from within, through its own rules and offices. Look for the sentence where the institution keeps running and nobody sees the attack happen.

Not quite! Subversion means the weakening or overthrowing of a system from within by quiet, indirect means, so it's not the correct choice here because these marchers do everything in the open — demands read aloud beneath the ministry's own windows are defiance, which announces itself, and subversion never does.

Not quite! Subversion means the weakening or overthrowing of a system from within by quiet, indirect means, so it's not the correct choice here because cut cables and loosened bolts are concrete physical damage to a structure — a saboteur's work on the bridge itself, not a quiet turning of any system's rules.

Not quite! Subversion means the weakening or overthrowing of a system from within by quiet, indirect means, so it's not the correct choice here because unfiled forms and sliding deadlines describe decay with no author — subversion is deliberate, and someone has to be doing the turning.
